questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: NADIR
questions.x: 'Nadir' is the opposite of 'Zenith'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Nadir'.

questions.q: The more you practise, ____ you become.
questions.x: Correct answer: the more confident. The comparative correlative 'the more…the more'.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To face the music' mean?
o: To accept the consequences of one's actions
questions.x: 'To face the music' means: to accept the consequences of one's actions.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: ENERVATE
questions.x: 'Enervate' means weaken. 'Energise' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Deference'.
questions.x: 'Deference' means respect. 'Contempt' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A person with refined taste in art, food or drink'
questions.x: 'Connoisseur' means a person with refined taste in art, food or drink.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To be at sixes and sevens'
o: To be in confusion or disorder
To be in the right place
questions.x: 'To be at sixes and sevens' means: to be in confusion or disorder.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Being a rainy day, / the office / closed early.
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'Being a rainy day'. Dangling participle: the office was not 'being a rainy day'. Rewrite: 'It being a rainy day, the office closed early'.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Verbose'.
questions.x: 'Verbose' is the opposite of 'Succinct'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Verbose'.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: DISCREET
questions.x: 'Discreet' means tactful. 'Indiscreet' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: According to the author, why may employers treat compliance as optional?
o: Workers do not want minimum wages
questions.x: Answer: 'Weak inspection and rare penalties'. Few inspectors, paper records and rare penalties make non-compliance tempting. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Good laws can fail through poor implementation. A statute may promise minimum wages to every worker, but if inspectors are few, records are kept on paper and penalties are rarely imposed, employers may calculate that compliance is optional. Digital records, random inspections and quick adjudication change this calculation. Enforcement is not about harassment; it is about making the honest employer's competitor pay the same costs.

questions.q: What does the author mean by 'making the honest employer's competitor pay the same costs'?
o: Enforcement creates a level playing field among employers
Honest employers should pay higher taxes
questions.x: Answer: 'Enforcement creates a level playing field among employers'. Enforcement ensures that non-compliant firms do not gain an unfair cost advantage. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Good laws can fail through poor implementation. A statute may promise minimum wages to every worker, but if inspectors are few, records are kept on paper and penalties are rarely imposed, employers may calculate that compliance is optional. Digital records, random inspections and quick adjudication change this calculation. Enforcement is not about harassment; it is about making the honest employer's competitor pay the same costs.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Lucknow Pact 2. Rowlatt Act 3. Surat Split 4. Partition of Bengal
questions.x: Partition of Bengal (1905), Surat Split (1907), Lucknow Pact (1916), Rowlatt Act (1919).

questions.q: The 'Temple Entry Proclamation' of 1936 was issued by the ruler of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Travancore. Maharaja Chithira Thirunal opened temples to all Hindus.

questions.q: Matangini Hazra, killed while leading a procession during the Quit India Movement, was from:
questions.x: Correct answer: Tamluk, Bengal. She was 73 years old and was called 'Gandhi Buri'.

questions.q: The 'Bhil uprisings' against British rule took place mainly in:
questions.x: Correct answer: Khandesh (western India). Bhils revolted repeatedly in 1817–19 and later.

questions.q: The Rowlatt Act (1919) was opposed because it:
questions.x: Correct answer: Allowed detention without trial. Gandhi called a nationwide hartal on 6 April 1919.

questions.q: Arrange the following Governor-Generals/Viceroys in chronological order: 1. Lord Lytton 2. Lord Canning 3. Lord Ripon 4. Lord Curzon

Consider the following statements about the Cripps Mission:
1. It was sent by the Churchill government.
2. The Congress accepted its proposals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
Both the Congress and the Muslim League rejected the proposals.

questions.q: The immediate cause of the Revolt of 1857 is often attributed to:
o: Greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle
questions.x: Rumours that the cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat offended both Hindu and Muslim sepoys.

questions.q: The 1940 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Ramgarh; it was the session after which no regular session met until 1946, Azad remaining president through the Quit India years.

questions.q: Ashwini Kumar Dutta is associated with the founding of:
questions.x: Ashwini Kumar Dutta founded the Swadesh Bandhab Samiti, Barisal.

questions.q: V. Narayanan took charge as the Chairman of ISRO in January 2025, succeeding:
questions.x: Correct answer: S. Somanath. He is a propulsion specialist from LPSC.

questions.q: 'DigiLocker' provides:
o: A cloud platform for issuing and storing authentic digital documents
questions.x: Correct answer: A cloud platform for issuing and storing authentic digital documents. Documents in DigiLocker are legally valid under IT rules.

questions.q: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries concerning:
questions.x: Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi were honoured. The 2024 prize was for microRNA.

questions.q: The headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization is located in:
questions.x: International Civil Aviation Organization: headquartered in Montreal.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 11 May?
o: National Statistics Day (birth anniversary of P. C. Mahalanobis)
questions.x: 11 May is National Technology Day (Pokhran-II tests, 1998).

questions.q: The 'Global Cybersecurity Index' is published by:
questions.x: 'Global Cybersecurity Index' is brought out by International Telecommunication Union.

questions.q: India won its first ICC Women's ODI World Cup in November 2025, defeating which team in the final at Navi Mumbai?
questions.x: Correct answer: South Africa. Harmanpreet Kaur captained the side.

questions.q: The 2036 Summer Olympics bid by India is being pursued with which city as the proposed host?
questions.x: Correct answer: Ahmedabad. India submitted a letter of intent to the IOC in 2024.

questions.q: After mass youth-led protests in September 2025, who became the interim Prime Minister of Nepal (the first woman to hold the post)?
questions.x: Correct answer: Sushila Karki. She was formerly Chief Justice of Nepal.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Dharma Guardian' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Dharma Guardian' is a bilateral exercise between India and Japan.

questions.q: The Constitution of India originally (1950) had how many Articles and Schedules?
questions.x: Over time, the number of Schedules has risen to 12 and Articles to over 460 (numbering retained at 395 with lettered insertions).

questions.q: The Constitution of India describes the official language of the Union as:
o: Hindi in Devanagari script, with international form of Indian numerals
questions.x: Article 343(1); English continues for official purposes under the Official Languages Act, 1963.

questions.q: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
questions.x: Correct answer: The Lok Sabha. Article 75(3).

questions.q: Lok Adalats were given statutory status under the:
questions.x: An award of a Lok Adalat is final and binding; no appeal lies against it.

questions.q: The anti-defection law disqualification decision is taken by the presiding officer, which is subject to judicial review as held in:
questions.x: The Court upheld the Tenth Schedule but held the Speaker's decision justiciable.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Right to Education under Article 21A covers children aged 6 to 14 years.
2. Article 45 now deals with early childhood care and education for children below six.
3. The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act was enacted in 2009.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three statements are correct.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Supreme Court to be a court of record"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 129.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment extended SC/ST reservation in legislatures and ended nomination of Anglo-Indian members?
questions.x: It was the 104th Amendment Act of 2020.

questions.q: The National Commission for Women was set up in 1992 as a:
o: Department of the Ministry of Home Affairs
questions.x: Correct answer: Statutory body. It was set up under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Facilities for instruction in mother tongue at primary stage"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 350A.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the state with the highest sex ratio is:
questions.x: Kerala had 1,084 females per 1,000 males; Haryana had the lowest among States.

questions.q: 'Inclusive growth' as an explicit objective was emphasised in the:
questions.x: The Eleventh Plan (2007–12) was titled 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'.

questions.q: Which committee/body is associated with "Review of domestic gas pricing"?
questions.x: Kirit Parikh Committee (2022) dealt with review of domestic gas pricing.

questions.q: India's largest services export category is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Software and IT-enabled services. Computer services dominate India's services exports.

questions.q: The National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023) targets production capacity of:
o: At least 5 million tonnes per annum by 2030
questions.x: Correct answer: At least 5 million tonnes per annum by 2030. It aims to make India a hub for green hydrogen.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 10% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹1000 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.1 = 10.
Total deposits = 1000 × 10 = ₹10,000 crore (of which new credit = ₹9,000 crore).

questions.q: Which of the following is included in India's GDP?
questions.x: Imputed rent is included; financial transactions and second-hand sales (except dealer margins) are not.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'qualitative' (selective) credit control tool of the RBI?
o: Margin requirements on loans against securities
questions.x: Quantitative tools affect overall credit; selective tools target specific sectors.

questions.q: The main thrust of the Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997–2002) was:
o: Self-reliant and self-generating economy; disrupted by wars and drought, followed by plan holidays
Rapid industrialisation with heavy industries, based on the Mahalanobis model
Growth with social justice and equity
questions.x: Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997–2002): Growth with social justice and equity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fifteenth Finance Commission:
1. It used 'demographic performance' as a criterion for horizontal devolution.
2. It recommended 41% of the divisible pool for States.
3. It was chaired by Y. V. Reddy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It was chaired by N. K. Singh; Y. V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC.

questions.q: A transaction completely left out of the books is an:
questions.x: Correct answer: Error of complete omission. It does not affect the trial balance.

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹85,000, closing inventory is ₹40,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹5,00,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (85,000 + 40,000) / 2 = ₹62,500.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 5,00,000 / 62,500 = 8 times.

questions.q: Salary outstanding at the year-end is recorded as:
o: Salary A/c Dr. To Outstanding Salary A/c
Salary A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
Cash A/c Dr. To Salary A/c
Outstanding Salary A/c Dr. To Salary A/c
questions.x: Correct answer: Salary A/c Dr. To Outstanding Salary A/c. The expense is recognised and a liability created.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹11,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹1,000; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹2,500; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹100. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹11,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 1,000
− Cheques deposited not credited 2,500
− Bank charges 100
Pass book balance = ₹9,400.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹1,40,000 is depreciated at 15% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 1,40,000 × (0.85)^3 = ₹85,977.50.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹77,000.)

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹40,000, Debtors ₹90,000, Inventory ₹20,000, Prepaid expenses ₹5,000, Creditors ₹20,000, Bills payable ₹10,000 and Outstanding expenses ₹10,000. Its quick (acid-test) ratio is:
questions.x:
Quick assets exclude inventory and prepaid expenses: 40,000 + 90,000 = ₹1,30,000.
Current liabilities = ₹40,000.
Quick ratio = 1,30,000 / 40,000 = 3.25 : 1 (benchmark 1 : 1).

questions.q: A firm earns an average profit of ₹71,600 on capital employed of ₹5,30,000. The normal rate of return in the industry is 12%. Goodwill at 4 years' purchase of super profit is:

A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹60,000 and at the end ₹1,30,000. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹15,000 and withdrew ₹15,000 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 1,30,000 + 15,000 − 15,000 − 60,000 = ₹70,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: Which accounting standard governs Property, Plant and Equipment for companies following Ind AS?
questions.x: Ind AS 16 corresponds to AS 10 (PPE); Ind AS 2 is inventories, Ind AS 7 cash flows and Ind AS 38 intangibles.

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 250 units @ ₹17; 10th — 150 units @ ₹18; 20th — 300 units @ ₹21. 500 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 200 units left come from the latest purchases: 200 × ₹21 = ₹4,200.

questions.q: Which of the following is revenue expenditure?
o: Installation charges of a new plant
questions.x: Correct answer: Routine repairs of machinery. Routine repairs maintain earning capacity and are charged to P&L.

questions.q: Under AS 9 / Ind AS 115 principles, revenue from sale of goods is recognised when:
o: Control (significant risks and rewards) passes to the buyer
questions.x: Correct answer: Control (significant risks and rewards) passes to the buyer. Ind AS 115 uses a five-step model based on transfer of control.

questions.q: Under GST, input tax credit paid on purchases is recorded in the books as:
o: An asset (Input CGST/SGST/IGST A/c), set off against output tax liability
questions.x: Output tax collected is a liability; ITC is an asset adjusted against it.

questions.q:
Consider the following items:
1. Purchase of a delivery van
2. Payment of electricity bill
3. Brokerage paid on purchase of land
4. Wages paid to workers for construction of a building
How many of the above are capital expenditure?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Items 1, 3 and 4 are capital expenditure; electricity bill is revenue.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court in Bangalore Water Supply (1978) held that sovereign functions of the State are excluded from 'industry'.
Reason (R): Under the IR Code, all activities of government departments are excluded from the definition of industry.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is correct — sovereign functions were excluded. R is false: the IR Code excludes sovereign functions and specified activities (defence research, atomic energy, space), not all government activities.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an 'unfair labour practice' on the part of an employer listed in the IR Code?
o: Taking disciplinary action against a worker after a fair domestic inquiry
Discharging a worker for filing charges under the Code
Interfering with workers' right to organise
questions.x: Disciplinary action after a fair inquiry is lawful; the others are listed unfair labour practices in the Second Schedule.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of a 'closed shop' arrangement (not recognised in Indian law)?
o: Only union members may be employed
questions.x: Closed shop requires union membership as a condition of employment; Indian law protects the freedom not to join a union.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, an employer in a non-Chapter X establishment with 50 or more workers who intends to close down must give notice to the government at least how many days before closure?
questions.x: Section 74 requires at least sixty days' notice of intended closure in establishments with fifty or more workers.

questions.q: The OSH Code subsumed the Working Journalists and Other Newspaper Employees Act, 1955. The OSH Code defines 'working journalist' to include:
o: Journalists working in electronic and digital media, besides newspapers
questions.x: The Code broadens 'working journalist' to cover electronic and digital media.

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, what is the purpose of a 'facilitator' notice before prosecution for a first-time contravention?
o: To authorise immediate arrest of the employer
To impose a lifetime ban on the business
To give the employer an opportunity to comply within a set time before prosecution
To require union approval for any action
questions.x: Inspector-cum-Facilitators must give an opportunity to comply within a specified period before launching prosecution for a first contravention, unless it is a repeat.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine branches of social security in ILO Convention No. 102?
questions.x: The nine branches are medical care, sickness, unemployment, old-age, employment injury, family, maternity, invalidity and survivors' benefits.

questions.q: The 15th Indian Labour Conference (1957) laid down norms for a need-based minimum wage. One of these norms is that the standard working-class family comprises:
o: Three consumption units for one earner
Five consumption units for two earners
questions.x: The norms assume three consumption units (earner, spouse, two children counted as one unit), 2,700 calories per adult, 72 yards of cloth per family per year, rent and 20% for fuel, lighting and miscellaneous.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about strikes under the IR Code:
1. A strike notice is required in all industrial establishments.
2. Mass casual leave by 50% or more workers on a day counts as a strike.
3. Strikes are allowed during the pendency of proceedings before an Industrial Tribunal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Strikes are prohibited during Tribunal proceedings and for 60 days after their conclusion.

questions.q: A worker earned ₹520 per day as basic + DA and has 12 years and 8 months of continuous service when retrenched. Retrenchment compensation under the IR Code is:
questions.x: 8 months exceeds six months, so service counts as 13 years. Compensation = 15 × 520 × 13 = ₹1,01,400.

questions.q: Alan Fox's analysis of 'frames of reference' (1966) contrasted which two perspectives?
questions.x: Fox's research paper for the Donovan Commission contrasted unitary and pluralist frames; he later developed a radical critique.

questions.q: In Uptron India Ltd v. Shammi Bhan (1998), the Supreme Court held that a standing order providing automatic termination for overstaying leave:
o: Must comply with natural justice before termination
Is always valid without any inquiry
questions.x: Following D.K. Yadav, the Court required an opportunity of hearing before termination.

questions.q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, compensation for death of an employee is computed as a percentage of monthly wages multiplied by a relevant factor. That percentage is:
questions.x: For death: 50% of monthly wages × relevant factor (or the prescribed minimum, whichever is more); for permanent total disablement it is 60%.

questions.q: Under the Contract Labour Act, 1970, abolition of contract labour in any process could be ordered by the appropriate government after consulting:
o: The Central or State Advisory Contract Labour Board
questions.x: Section 10 empowered the government, after consulting the Advisory Board, to prohibit contract labour considering whether the work is perennial and incidental to the main activity.

questions.q: 'Hunger strike' and 'token strike' differ in that a token strike is:
o: A short-duration strike to register protest
questions.x: Token strikes last for a short period (e.g., a day) to signal grievance.

questions.q: An establishment retrenches 4 workers whose last drawn wages are ₹600 per day each. Its contribution to the Worker Re-skilling Fund will be:
questions.x: 15 days' wages per worker = 15 × 600 = ₹9,000; for 4 workers = ₹36,000.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY), now closed for new subscriptions, was implemented through:
o: LIC, providing assured pension to senior citizens aged 60+
questions.x: PMVVY (2017) offered assured returns via LIC; it was open until 31 March 2023.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about social security in India:
1. Most of India's workforce is in informal employment without comprehensive social security.
2. e-Shram is meant to build a database of unorganised workers.
3. ESI coverage is available to all workers irrespective of wages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
ESI has a wage ceiling (₹21,000/month); the other statements are correct.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 26 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹830. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 26-week period including Sundays: 26 × 7 = 182 days.
Amount = ₹830 × 182 = ₹1,51,060. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹1,29,480.)

questions.q: An insured employee earns gross wages of ₹11,500 in a month. What is the total ESI contribution (employer + employee) payable for that month?
questions.x:
Employee share 0.75% = ₹86.25 → ₹87; employer share 3.25% = ₹373.75 → ₹374 (rounded up to the next rupee).
Total = ₹461 (4% of wages; rates in force since 1 July 2019).

questions.q: Under the Code on Social Security, social security benefits for building and other construction workers are financed mainly through:
o: A cess on the cost of construction
questions.x: The BOCW cess (1–2% of construction cost) is collected and used by State welfare boards.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of scheme and nature:
1. EPF — defined contribution
2. EPS 1995 — defined benefit
3. NPS — defined contribution
4. Unified Pension Scheme — assured payout
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.x:
4 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
All four pairs are correctly matched.

questions.q: Under EPS 1995, a member with 20 or more years of pensionable service gets a weightage (service bonus) of:
questions.x: Two years are added to pensionable service for members with 20 or more years of contributory service retiring on superannuation.

questions.q: The assured minimum pension under the Unified Pension Scheme for an employee with at least 10 years of service is:
questions.x: UPS guarantees a minimum of ₹10,000 a month on superannuation after at least ten years of service.

questions.q: An employee's basic + DA is ₹30,000 a month and EPF contributions are paid on actual wages. The employer's EPF account share (after EPS) per month is:
questions.x: Employer's 12% = ₹3,600; EPS capped at ₹1,250; EPF share = ₹3,600 − ₹1,250 = ₹2,350.

questions.q: Under the EPF Scheme, the 'Electronic Return' discloses each member's wages and contributions; non-filing exposes the employer to:
o: Penal action and damages along with recovery
questions.x: Failure to file returns or pay dues attracts penalties under Section 14 and damages under 14B.

questions.q: Under the liberalised EPF partial-withdrawal norms approved in October 2025, members must always retain what share of contributions as minimum balance?
questions.x: A 25% minimum balance must be maintained so that members continue to earn interest and build retirement savings.

questions.q: The 'Coal Mines Provident Fund Organisation' (CMPFO), separate from EPFO, administers PF and pension for:
questions.x: CMPFO, headquartered at Dhanbad, administers the Coal Mines PF and Pension Schemes.

questions.q: In computing, 'MAC (address)' stands for:
questions.x: MAC (address) = Media Access Control.

questions.q: World Wide Web is credited to:
questions.x: World Wide Web: Tim Berners-Lee.

questions.q: Hard water contains dissolved salts of:
questions.x: Temporary hardness (bicarbonates) is removed by boiling; permanent hardness needs washing soda or ion exchange.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to securely transmit web pages?
questions.x: HTTPS uses TLS encryption (padlock icon).

questions.q: Which of the following is a biofertiliser?
questions.x: Azotobacter, Rhizobium and blue-green algae fix nitrogen.

questions.q: Which organ is primarily affected by hepatitis?
questions.x: Hepatitis B and C can cause chronic liver disease.

questions.q: The hexadecimal number 'FF' equals which decimal number?
The normal blood pressure of a healthy adult is about:
questions.x: Correct answer: 120/80 mm Hg. Systolic/diastolic pressure.

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'Simple Mail Transfer Protocol'?
questions.x: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol is abbreviated as SMTP.

questions.q: The 'Candela' is the SI unit of:
questions.x: Candela measures luminous intensity.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
questions.x: Solar, wind, hydro and biomass are renewable.

questions.q: 'Phishing' emails can often be identified by:
o: Urgent requests to click links or share passwords from unfamiliar or spoofed senders
Messages from known colleagues about meetings
Calendar invites from HR on official domains
questions.x: Correct answer: Urgent requests to click links or share passwords from unfamiliar or spoofed senders. Always verify the sender's domain and never share credentials.

questions.q: A vessel holds 120 litres of pure milk. 12 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 120 × (1 − 12/120)² = 120 × (0.9)² = 97.2 litres.
Removing 2 × 12 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a storage tank in 5 hours and 20 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(5, 20, 12) = 60 units.
Rates: +12, +3, −5 units/hour → net 10 units/hour.
Time = 60 / 10 = 6 hours.

questions.q: Team X can verify a batch of claims in 36 days and Team Y in 72 days. They start together, but Team X leaves after 21 days. In how many days in all is the work completed?
questions.x:
Work done together in 21 days = 21 × (1/36 + 1/72) = 21/24 = 7/8.
Remaining = 1/8, done by Team Y alone in 1/8 × 72 = 9 days.
Total = 21 + 9 = 30 days.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 8 : 9. After 8 years, the ratio will become 48 : 53. What is P's present age?
On which day of the week did 28 May 1935 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 1934: 1600 years → 0 odd days; 300 years → 1; remaining 34 years have 8 leap + 26 ordinary → 8×2 + 26 = 42 → 0 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 1935 up to 28 May = 148 → 1 odd day(s).
Total = 1 + 0 + 1 = 2 → 2 → Tuesday.

questions.q: A bag has 6 white and 7 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(7,2)/C(13,2) = 21/78.
Required = 1 − 7/26 = 19/26.

questions.q: Find the remainder when 3^128 is divided by 9.
The average of 11 observations is 46. The average of the first 6 is 47 and that of the last 6 is 46. The 6th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 11 = 11 × 46 = 506.
First 6 + last 6 = 6×47 + 6×46 = 558; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 558 − 506 = 52.

questions.q: A starts a business with ₹20,000. B joins after 6 months with ₹60,000, and C joins after 7 months with ₹35,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹1,08,500, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 20,000×12, B: 60,000×6, C: 35,000×5 → 48 : 72 : 35.
B's share = 72/155 × 1,08,500 = ₹50,400.

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 82, 138, 264 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 138 − 82 = 56, 264 − 138 = 126.
HCF(56, 126) = 14.

questions.q: At what time between 8 and 9 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
questions.x:
At 8:00 the minute hand is 40 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To coincide it must gain 40 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 40 × 60/55 = 480/11 minutes = 43 7/11 minutes past 8.

questions.q: At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 6 years. In how many years will it become 3 times itself at the same rate?
questions.x:
Doubling means interest = 1 × principal in 6 years, i.e. rate = 100/6 = 16.67% p.a.
To become 3 times, interest must be 2 × principal.
Time = (2 × 100) / 16.67 = 12 years. (Rule: time ∝ number of times the principal is earned as interest.)

questions.q: A bus runs from town P to town Q at 80 km/h and returns along the same road at 120 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.x:
For equal distances, average speed = 2uv/(u + v) (harmonic mean), not (u + v)/2.
= 2 × 80 × 120 / (80 + 120) = 19200/200 = 96 km/h.

questions.q: Find the unit digit of 34^111 + 82^49.
questions.x:
Only last digits matter.
Unit digit of first term (base ending 4, cycle 4,6,4,6; 111 → position 3) = 4.
Unit digit of second term (base ending 2, cycle 2,4,8,6; 49 → position 1) = 2.
4 + 2 → unit digit 6.
